clue.text: Roger brought before the beak over drawing back a curtain

indicators.note: drawing something back pulls it the other way, so the built string is read from its end

parts.note: 'had up' means summoned to court; a beak is slang for a magistrate
R is Roger in radio-speak

explanation.surface: Someone hauled before a magistrate for pulling open a curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes over into the middle of HAD UP, giving HADRUP, which read backwards is PURDAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Purdah is the screen used in parts of South Asia to keep women out of sight of men.

clue.text: Wearer of trousers lacking sort of turn-up?

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
to lack something is to be without it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written; the answer sitting inside it is a coincidence of the deletion, not a hidden word
taken as written; these are the letters stripped out

explanation.surface: A man asking about trousers without turn-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: 'sort' turned up gives TROS, and those letters (TRO at the front, S at the end) are removed from TROUSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wears clothes puts them to use, so a person employing an item is its user.

clue.text: Nice doctor shortly produced a pharmacological essence

indicators.note: said shortly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
produced suggests made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; the French city is a decoy
doctor without its last letter

explanation.surface: A doctor from Nice has made up a medicinal extract.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoction is a concentrated liquid made by boiling down plant material, as in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Car case for carcase?

parts.note: surface reading: a container for a motor vehicle, a wordplay jingle
setter's reading: a vehicle that encloses a dead body on its way to burial

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyming jingle of car, case and carcase hides a funeral vehicle; carcase is an old spelling of carcass, a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the funeral vehicle that carries a coffin and the corpse inside it.

clue.text: Bile gland trouble can be shocking

parts.note: the liver is the organ that produces bile
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A liver complaint that could give one a nasty surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing the answer: a live rail is the electrified rail on a railway, which delivers an electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A live rail carries electric current to power trains, so touching it gives an electric shock.

clue.text: Putting consideration to one side may provide a solution

definitions.note: a description of what the answer does rather than a synonym

parts.note: lateral means at or towards the side
consideration is careful thought

explanation.surface: Setting careful thought aside might crack the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as advice to stop thinking, but taken piece by piece it is sideways thought, the noted problem-solving method.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking is creative problem solving from an unexpected angle, a method that can produce answers.

clue.text: Old migrant making call on hospital without leave

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a call is a short visit
to leave is to go
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone paying a visit to a hospital while absent without leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without leave' reads like absence without permission, but 'without' is the old word for outside; 'on' in a down clue puts the hospital below.
explanation.definitionFit: The Visigoths were a Germanic people who migrated across the late Roman Empire into Gaul and Spain.

clue.text: Parts dealt to the loser

indicators.note: dealt like cards, which are shuffled before dealing, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The weakest player gets the smallest share.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts in a play or film are the roles assigned to actors.

clue.text: Awkwardness of canine leg bent at bottom of pole

indicators.note: something bent is out of its proper shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of pole

explanation.surface: A dog cocks its leg clumsily at the foot of a lamp post.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegance is a lack of grace or polish, the clumsy quality of awkwardness.

clue.text: Inclination to give a swan song?

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: Wanting to perform a swan song, a final farewell performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan song' is a set phrase for a last performance, but the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or leaning towards something, a taste or bent.

clue.text: You are failed lovers!

indicators.note: failed suggests broken down, so the letters fall apart and reform

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An accusation thrown at a pair of unsuccessful romantics.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter addresses the reader: the person reading this clue is the one doing the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The person tackling the crossword is its solver, so the setter can address the reader as such.

clue.text: Tries charges of fiddling the till

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so the letters are messed about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is prosecuted for stealing from the shop takings.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is the machine in a shop that records sales and holds the money taken.

clue.text: A certain point, of course, where the man is in danger with no one about

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside

parts.note: peril is danger
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: about as in turned about, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: no plus I for one

explanation.surface: A spot on a route where a man is put at risk with no one around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' means on an orbital course, which is why the definition is so vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Perihelion is the spot in a planet's or comet's orbit nearest the sun, a specific location on its path.

clue.text: The priest is wrong to put the last first

indicators.note: the final letter is taken from the end and moved to the front

parts.note: evil is moral wrong

explanation.surface: A cleric is criticised for reversing the biblical order of last and first.
explanation.walkthrough: It echoes the Gospel line 'the last shall be first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was founder of the Hebrew priestly tribe, the Levites, so the name stands for a priest.

clue.text: Church following the lunar cycle?

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so the letters are churned into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A church that sets its calendar by the moon's phases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a link word, but 'Church following' together means a member of a denomination.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lutheran belongs to the Protestant denomination founded on Martin Luther's teaching.

clue.text: A bolt, perhaps in ironwork

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: split in two: iron is a chemical element, and op (opus) is a work

explanation.surface: A metal bolt set in a piece of ironwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironwork' must be split into iron and work, the second going inside the first. A bolt here is a sudden running away, not a piece of hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run off suddenly, and an elopement is running off secretly to marry.

clue.text: State where we feel separation from our island

parts.note: to miss someone is to feel their absence
taken as written
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A place where we feel homesick for our island home.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Diabolical ally is dropping King Henry the First

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an ally is a friend
R for Rex, king; this is the letter removed
taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a name is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Henry

explanation.surface: A wicked friend abandons King Henry I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Henry the First' reads as one monarch, but King is R taken out of FRIEND, and Henry the First is just H.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means devilishly cruel or wicked, like a fiend or demon.

clue.text: Weight not acceptable as in the past

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is left out

parts.note: an ounce is an imperial weight
U means acceptable, upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A measure of weight that used to be allowed but no longer is.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'acceptable' comes from the old U and non-U labels for upper-class and other speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some former time, formerly, as in 'once upon a time'.

clue.text: Some young ladies not up to college…

indicators.note: some of something is only part of it, so the word is cut short

parts.note: girls are young ladies

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some young women are not good enough for university.
explanation.walkthrough: Girton is a Cambridge college, founded as the first residential college for women, which suits the young ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: Girton College is one of the colleges making up the University of Cambridge.

clue.text: Abandons network for making trains late?

parts.note: leaves means abandons
online means connected to a network

explanation.surface: Someone quitting the internet, and railway delays.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves on the line is the notorious British excuse for delayed trains, when fallen autumn leaves make rails slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen autumn leaves on the railway tracks reduce grip and are blamed for British train delays.

clue.text: … possibly active in vice ring?

indicators.note: the second item is placed inside the first

parts.note: taken as written
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Continuing the college scene: perhaps involved in a criminal ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Active is one grammatical voice of a verb, the other being passive.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, voice is the verb category of which active and passive are examples.

clue.text: Drink said to give bodily support

indicators.note: said points to the word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: beer is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink that is claimed to strengthen the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the stand or frame on which a corpse or coffin rests before burial.

clue.text: A place by the motorway in the middle of France

definitions.note: milieu is the French word for middle

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, written as MI
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: A spot beside a motorway somewhere in central France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just means next to. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, Britain's first.
explanation.definitionFit: In French, milieu means middle; in English it has come to mean social setting or environment.

clue.text: Brave one died after Pinter play

indicators.note: after places the preceding pieces second, behind the rearranged name
playing with something means moving its parts around freely

parts.note: taken as written; Harold Pinter is the playwright
I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A courageous actor who died after appearing in a Pinter play.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter wrote plays, so 'Pinter play' reads as one of his works; here play signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and bold, a synonym for brave or daring.

clue.text: Common attitude among church people?

parts.note: surface reading: an opinion or outlook widely shared
setter's reading: attitude as bodily posture, the one worshippers adopt in prayer

explanation.walkthrough: Attitude can mean a physical position of the body, not just an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchgoers commonly get down on their knees to pray, a usual posture of worship.

clue.text: Tea urn for brewing essence

indicators.note: brewing stirs and mixes ingredients, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tea urn used to make the essence of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The nature of a thing is its basic character, its inherent quality.
